statement.text:
Do there exist infinite groups all of whose proper subgroups are cyclic of
order p that do not satisfy any nontrivial group identity except xp = 1 and its conse-
quences?
    Note that there exist infinite groups all of whose proper subgroups are infinite
cyclic that do not satisfy any nontrivial group identity (due to A. Olshanskii; see
P. Zusmanovich, J. Algebra, 388 (2013), 268–286, Remark after Theorem 6.1).
                                                                        P. Zusmanovich
